assumptions: Every acquisition was run with the same bead kit spiked in, so the beads are a constant signal over time.
The files are acquisitions of one panel, normalized to one baseline.
limits: Writing the normalized files is done from the panel; this door returns the beads, slopes and baseline.
bio.jane/contract.question: How much did the instrument's sensitivity drift over these acquisitions, and what are the counts with that drift taken out?

description: CATALYST normCytof bead normalization of mass cytometry acquisitions in the project, together: the beads found in every file (positive on each bead channel of the kit, negative on DNA Ir191/Ir193, by debarcoding with an estimated cutoff, then trimmed to within a number of MADs of each channel's median), each bead channel smoothed by a running median over acquisition time, each bead's least-squares slope to the baseline (the beads' mean counts) interpolated over time, and every event's counts multiplied by its slope.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

k.description: the running median's window in beads (made odd, capped at the bead count).

kit.description: the bead kit: EQ four-element beads (Ce140, Eu151, Eu153, Ho165, Lu175) or beta beads. Values: dvs (EQ four-element), beta (beta).

samples.description: the acquisitions normalized together, by name or id, comma-separated; empty for every FCS file in the project.

trim.description: beads further than this many MADs from their channel's median are not used.

name: normalize_cytof_beads

baseline.description: per bead channel, the beads' mean counts every acquisition was normalized to

files.description: per acquisition: its events, the beads found in it and the events removed with them
